subject: Streaming chunk loss — temporary degrade & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming chunk loss — temporary degrade & mitigation plan

Hi Alex / Lumen ops team,

We’re reaching out because we’ve detected truncated or missing chunks for long streaming responses on the hosted streaming endpoint (us-west-2) that may affect your document-generation flows. Timeline and current status: 
- Incident start: ~2026-08-19 08:45 UTC (observability alert p99_stream_drop).
- Impact: intermittent missing chunks in streamed responses; final completion tokens present in non-streamed requests.
- Scope: subset of long-session clients using the streaming WebSocket/HTTP SSE path (we see increased errors from your account).

Immediate mitigation we can apply for you now (manual, low-risk):
1) Route calls to the non-streaming endpoint (same model) by setting streaming=false — this returns full responses in a single payload and avoids chunk reassembly.
2) As an alternative, enable the temporary chunk-retry header (X-Redwood-Chunk-Retry: 1) which forces the runtime to request missing frames when detected.

We’ve attached a short log snippet showing dropped frame ids for one of your sessions (streaming-log-snippet.txt).

Questions for you:
- Can we temporarily toggle your traffic to non-streaming while we roll a mitigation? We can do this for you immediately if you confirm.
- Are you running a client-side retry/merge that would be compatible with the chunk-retry header?

We’ve opened incident INC-2026-0819 on the status page (https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0819) and the on-call team is engaged. I’m cc’ing engineering/ops to propose next steps and a fix ETA.

Thanks — we’ll keep this thread updated as we have milestones.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: streaming-log-snippet.txt (text), links to status page"

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lumenhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming chunk loss — temporary degrade & mitigation plan

Thanks Soojin — we can confirm a handful of user sessions showed mid-stream truncation starting around 08:48 UTC. Our product team just flagged a high-priority support ticket; it’s impacting one customer-facing feature where we stream multi-paragraph clinical summaries.

Please proceed to route our traffic to non-streaming for the next 60 minutes while you apply the fix. We’d also like an ETA for when normal streaming will be safe again; the feature relies on low-latency streaming for UX.

Alex
VP, Engineering — Lumen Health
alex.turner@lumenhealth.com

Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming chunk loss — temporary degrade & mitigation plan

Soojin / team — brief technical summary and proposed remediation plan below.

Observed behavior:
- The streaming multiplexer occasionally drops subframe packets when eviction and KV cache flushes coincide with concurrent long-lived sessions; sequence numbers are not re-associated with the parent stream under heavy memory pressure. This results in missing intermediate chunks though finalization tokens are often generated by the backend.

Immediate actions (in-flight):
1) I will push a staged hotfix to the streaming multiplexer (v2.2.3) that enforces an in-memory sequence checkpoint and disables the aggressive eviction path for long sessions. Target rollout start: 10:20 PDT, staggered across us-west-2 AZs.
2) Update routing rule for Lumen Health to non-streaming (as requested) — Soojin, you can toggle on our internal account bypass; I'll add a safety TTL of 30 mins.
3) Increase the runtime stream buffer cap from 64MB to 128MB for affected pools as a temporary measure.

Customer note for status page (proposed):
"We are investigating intermittent missing data in streaming responses for a subset of users in our US region. We have applied a temporary routing change for affected customers and are deploying a hotfix to resolve packet reassembly under high memory pressure. We will provide a full post-incident report once validated."

Attachments: mitigation-runbook.pdf (runbook with rollout steps, verification checks, rollback instructions).

I will post deployment progress here. If we see any unexpected regressions, we will pause the rollout and escalate.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal Platform Engineer, Serving Runtime
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Incident update: streaming chunk loss — incident mitigated; postmortem scheduled

Alex — follow-up and final customer-facing summary.

Status: mitigated (US region - us-west-2).
What we changed:
- Deployed multiplexer hotfix v2.2.3 to streaming pools in us-west-2 (rolled 3 AZs, canary -> full).
- Temporary routing change applied for your account routing streaming requests to non-streaming with a 30-minute TTL while rollout completed.
- Increased stream buffer cap to 128MB to reduce eviction pressure during long sessions.

Impact summary:
- Incident window: 2026-08-19 08:45 UTC -> 2026-08-20 15:10 UTC (final verification).
- Affected customers: subset of users on streaming endpoints; Lumen Health experienced truncated streaming responses for multi-paragraph summaries (confirmed).
- Severity: elevated (transient data loss in-stream).

Next steps and follow-up:
- We will publish a full post-incident report by 2026-08-27 with root cause analysis and permanent mitigations (kernel-level guardrails and additional stream validated tests).
- Internal action: add streaming end-to-end tests for long-session reassembly; revise evictions policy.
- If you want the routing change reversed earlier, reply and we’ll coordinate a short verification window.

Apologies for the disruption — we know streaming latency and fidelity are important for your UX. Please reach out on this thread if you see any residual anomalies; we’ll keep monitoring your traffic closely over the next 48 hours.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: mitigation-runbook.pdf, streaming-log-snippet.txt
